---
title: "Reading and rewriting a file in a pipe empties it"
ref: PIP-05
categories: [Pipes]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'readLines(f) |> gsub(...) |> write(file = f)'
reponse: '""'
attendu: "`\"something\"`"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2025)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
f <- tempfile()
write("temp", file = f)

readLines(f) |>
  gsub(pattern = "temp", replacement = "something", x = _) |>
  write(file = f)

readLines(f)
```
:::

## Why

The pipe does not read the file before writing it: it builds the call `write(gsub(..., readLines(f)), file = f)`. Because of lazy evaluation, `write()` starts by opening its destination file, which empties it, and only evaluates its first argument when it is time to write. `readLines()` then reads a file that is already empty.

## The fix

Force the read before the write, by going through a variable.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
write("temp", file = f)
content <- readLines(f)
content <- gsub(pattern = "temp", replacement = "something", x = content)
write(content, file = f)
readLines(f)
```
:::
